rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken adverbial for doing something well or in a pleasing way.

example.english: We worked together fine and got it sorted in the end.
example.traditional: 我哋好好咁合作，最後都搞掂喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hou2 hou2 gam2 hap6 zok3 zeoi3 hau6 dou1 gaau2 dim6 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for a fine imposed as punishment for breaking the law.

example.english: They got a fine of five hundred dollars for illegal parking.
example.traditional: 佢因為亂泊車，畀人罰款五百蚊。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jan1 wai6 lyun6 paak3 ce1 bei2 jan4 fat6 fun2 ng5 baak3 man1

rows.note: This is the everyday all-purpose verb for imposing a monetary penalty on someone.

example.english: If you keep parking recklessly, the management will fine you.
example.traditional: 你再亂咁泊車，管理處就會罰錢㗎喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 zoi3 lyun6 gam2 bok6 ce1 gun2 lei5 cyu3 zau6 wui5 fat6 cin2 gaa3 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something is okay, satisfactory, or that you are doing fine.

example.english: I'm doing fine now, so you don't need to worry.
example.traditional: 我而家幾好，你唔使擔心。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 gei2 hou2 nei5 m4 sai2 daam1 sam1

rows.note: Use this for particles or pieces that are very small and for things such as threads that are particularly thin.

example.english: This thread is very fine, so it is easy to thread a needle.
example.traditional: 呢條線好幼細，穿針都方便。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 sin3 hou2 jau3 sai3 cyun1 zam1 dou1 fong1 bin6

rows.note: Use this when fine means superior in quality rather than merely acceptable.

example.english: The steaks at this restaurant are really fine.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳啲牛扒真係高質。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 ngau4 paa2 zan1 hai6 gou1 zat1

rows.note: Use this when fine means good-looking or attractive, especially of a person.

example.jyutping: keoi5 go3 neoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 leng3
